title: User Vault: the credential is injected at request time
lede: An agent asks for an operation. The gateway reads only the caller's own vault, unseals the credential and injects it. The agent never sees it and the backend logs who actually acted. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

nodes.label: Key provider (AWS KMS, Vault or development key; mock)

edges.label: inject it (bearer, key, Basic or headers)

steps.title: The agent asks
steps.what: The agent asks the gateway for an operation on {{castT1}}. It holds no credential.

steps.title: Caller's own vault only
steps.what: The gateway looks in the vault of the caller, and nowhere else: there is no way to name another vault.

steps.title: The key unseals it
steps.what: The data key, resolved at startup from AWS Secrets Manager with KMS, or Vault, or the development key as fallback, opens the sealed value.

steps.title: Credential to gateway
steps.what: The plaintext lives in memory for this call and is never returned by any API.

steps.title: Injected into backend
steps.what: The gateway builds the Authorization or header form for the entry's shape and sends it.

steps.title: Backend logs who acted
steps.what: The backend identifies the caller from the credential itself, so its log names {{castUser}}, not a shared account.

steps.title: Answer to the agent
steps.what: Only the answer goes back. The agent never learned the credential.
